architecture: BullMQ workers on Redis: one processor module per queue, fed by public intake endpoints and internal schedulers, with a pino logger, an HMAC-signed control-plane callback and provisioning helpers

cases.architecture: BullMQ processor decoding payloads enqueued verbatim by a public intake endpoint
cases.why: Payloads arrive on this queue exactly as the public intake endpoint received them. The v2 branch parses JSON, but anything without that marker goes to node-serialize's unserialize, which reconstructs functions from the payload and invokes them: a caller who can post to the intake endpoint runs code in the worker.

cases.architecture: BullMQ processor decoding payloads enqueued verbatim by a public intake endpoint
cases.why: The same dependency is still installed and still used, but only to serialise a receipt the worker itself produces; both decode branches of the untrusted payload go through JSON.parse, which cannot instantiate behaviour.

cases.architecture: BullMQ processor holding OAuth tokens in its job payload, with a redaction helper
cases.why: The redaction helper is written, tested by use on the happy path, and then skipped in the failure branch, which logs the raw job payload — the mailbox access token and refresh token included — into a log stream that is shipped off the host and retained far longer than the tokens live.

cases.architecture: BullMQ processor holding OAuth tokens in its job payload, with a redaction helper
cases.why: The failure branch still logs the job for diagnosis and still reads the same token-bearing payload, but it passes it through the redaction helper and narrows the error to its message and code.

cases.architecture: BullMQ processor signing control-plane callbacks with an HMAC key read from the environment
cases.why: The signing key reads from the environment first, which is why nobody notices the literal: any deployment that forgets the variable signs its control-plane callbacks with a key that is in the repository, and anyone with read access to the source can forge a provisioning callback for any tenant. The two neighbouring fallbacks are a queue prefix and a public URL, so the pattern itself is not the problem.

cases.architecture: BullMQ processor signing control-plane callbacks with an HMAC key read from the environment
cases.why: The module still declares its configuration as constants with `||` fallbacks, but the fallbacks left are a queue prefix and a public control-plane URL; the signing key comes from a helper that throws at load time when the variable is missing, so there is nothing secret in the file.
